Some forest lands along the proposed Bad Creek-to-Oconee line right-of-way would be cleared to maintain proper line clearance. In mountainous terrain, selective clearing would be used to the fullest extent possible to maintain line clearance, and long-span towers would be used to cross valleys between mountain ridges, alleviating the need to clear all vegetation from beneath the lines. Applicant states that the present data show that they would be able to span the entire Howard Creek ravine with the proposed transmission line, thus minimizing the impact on water quality. Where forest lands are cleared, the Applicant would fertilize and revegetate transmission line right-of-way immediately with plants such as fesque, German millet, sericea lespedeza, and other vegetation suitable as cover and as food for wildlife.
Where the 525-kV line parallels or crosses Lake Keowee and streams, towers would be located far enough away from the water's edge to avoid runoff problems.
Low growing vegetation at the water's edge would not be disturbed, thus maintaining soil stability. In the more mountainous area near Bad Creek, forested areas on both sides of the streams would be left intact to maintain watershed protection.
In planning the Bad Creek transmission facilities, the use of common corridors for multiple lines has been planned to reduce the number of right-of-way corridors.
Solid and liquid construction wastes would be handled in accordance with applicable Government regulations. Care would be taken to prohibit the discharge of any undesirable chemicals or wastes during the operation of the project.
During construction of the project dams, water from the Bad Creek basin would be routed through a pipe beneath the main dam and would flow down the remaining 600 to 700 feet of Bad Creek, emptying into Howard Creek.
Applicant proposes to construct a flow augmentation system with a multilevel intake in the upper reservoir. The intake levels would be at elevations of 2,280, 2,230, and 2,120 feet (30, 80, and 190 feet below full pool elevation, respectively).
